name: Fable Unconstrained
strategy: Dual-momentum: long the 6-month sector/asset leaders that are not in a sharp 1-month correction - the Hormuz-driven energy complex (XLE, XOP, upstream COP, refiners VLO and MPC) and healthcare (XLV plus leader LLY) - with BTC cut after it failed the rule; every leg stop-protected, no leverage, 39% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: Research this week (web search plus a Yahoo daily-price pull as of the 10-23 close) confirms the regime the book was built for a week ago and sharpens it. Tape: Brent settled $116.72 on 10-23 (highest since April) after Iran said seven tankers were hit in Hormuz on 10-22 and reports that the US/Israel may strike Iran as soon as this weekend; the 10-year is 4.99%, the Fed (Chair Warsh) hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September with minutes pointing to another hike by year-end, the 10-28 FOMC is priced ~83% hold; VIX 19.45; S&P 7,623 and down four of the last six weeks on AI/semis weakness. My 6-month momentum screen ranks refiners first (MPC +104%, VLO +78%, PSX +74%), then LLY +44%, then the crude complex (DBE, USO, CVX, COP, XOM, XLE, XOP all at 6-month highs, 1-month +10-18%), XLV +24%, UNH, BRK-B; laggards are gold/silver/miners, uranium, copper, China and semis (SMH -21% off its high, 1-month -12%). Two changes. (1) BTC is cut: 6-month +4.7% trails SPY (+6.4%), 1-month -3.9%, 6.4% off its high, US spot-ETF flows net negative for October with a $636M outflow on 10-22 - that is not a leader under the rule, and the leg sat at -0.95%. (2) Its 10% is redeployed into two leaders the screen says qualify and the book did not own: LLY 5% (healthcare's single largest momentum name, 2.5% off its high; it reports 10-29, which is event risk but the rule does not sidestep earnings) and COP 5% (pure upstream at a 6-month high, the most direct equity beneficiary of a $116 Brent, reports 11-5). Refiners stay: VLO printed $23.90 adj EPS and $8.8B refining operating income on 10-22 and sold off 4% as the market priced peak margins, MPC reports 11-3; both are still +12-18% on the month so the 1-month correction rule does not fire, but I tighten their stops to 10% off the new fill with a 25% take-profit so a peak-margin unwind is cut early rather than ridden down 15%. XLE/XOP/XLV weights are unchanged. Risk: 46% of the book is now energy and the single tail that hurts it is a Hormuz reopening or ceasefire (crude fell 12% in a day in April); 12% stops on every energy leg and 39% cash at 4% are the answer, not a smaller allocation, because the rule says own the leader. Churn cost on the resize is a few basis points.

positions.thesis: Core energy-sector sleeve, unchanged at 15%: XLE is +21.9% over 6 months, +11.2% over 1 month and closed 10-23 at a fresh 6-month high ($69.33) with Brent at $116.72 on renewed Hormuz tanker attacks. It is the broadest, lowest-beta way to own the regime's leading sector (XOM/CVX ~40% of the fund, both at highs). 12% stop protects against a ceasefire-driven crude collapse like April's.

E&P beta sleeve, unchanged at 8%: XOP +20.0% over 6 months, +10.4% over 1 month, at a 6-month high ($201.69). Higher sensitivity to crude than XLE, which is what a dual-momentum book wants while crude is the leading asset; 12% stop caps the reopening tail.

New 5% leg funded by the BTC cut. ConocoPhillips is +23.9% over 6 months, +17.7% over 1 month and closed 10-23 at a 6-month high ($150.80) - the strongest 1-month momentum of the large caps in the complex and the purest large-cap upstream exposure to a $116 Brent. Reports 11-5 (consensus $2.69 vs $1.61 a year ago). Sized small because XLE/XOP already carry integrated and E&P exposure; 12% stop, 30% take-profit.

Refiner leg kept at 8% with a tighter stop. VLO is +77.8% over 6 months and +11.6% over 1 month, so the 1-month-correction rule does not fire, but it fell ~4% on 10-22 despite a record quarter ($23.90 adj EPS, refining operating income $8.8B vs $1.6B a year ago) as the market priced peak cracks, and is 8.8% off its high. Stop tightened to 10% off the 10-26 fill (from 15%) with a 25% take-profit so a margin-normalisation unwind is cut quickly.

Refiner leg kept at 8% with a tighter stop. MPC is the single strongest 6-month name in the screen (+104%) and still +17.7% over 1 month, 5.7% off its high after sympathy selling on VLO's print. Q2 refining margin was $36.33/bbl and it reports 11-3 (Citi $25.64 vs consensus $26.21) - same peak-margin event risk as VLO, so stop tightened to 10% with a 25% take-profit.

Healthcare sleeve unchanged at 12%: XLV is +24.3% over 6 months, +6.2% over 1 month, 1.1% off its high ($179.28) - the only non-energy sector that qualifies as a leader, driven by LLY (~14% of fund) and a re-rating of managed care after UNH's beat-and-raise on 10-13. Defensive ballast against the energy concentration; 12% stop.

New 5% leg funded by the BTC cut. Eli Lilly is the fourth-strongest name in the whole screen (+44.1% over 6 months, +10.6% over 1 month, 2.5% off its high at $1,273) and the largest healthcare momentum leader, which the book owned only indirectly through XLV. It reports Q3 on 10-29 (consensus roughly $9.6-9.8 vs $7.02 a year ago); the rule owns leaders through earnings, and the 5% size plus 12% stop bounds a miss. 30% take-profit.
